propositions: git fetch hangs indefinitely on byte-starved connections because _fetch_origin builds git argv without http.lowSpeedLimit / http.lowSpeedTime, leaving only a 300s wall-clock timeout as the abort mechanism.
A stalled connection (established but sending zero bytes) should abort in ~10 seconds via throughput-keyed abort, not burn the 300s ceiling.
A legitimately slow but progressing fetch (e.g. 2000 B/s dribble over a large clone) must not be aborted; the abort threshold is keyed on throughput floor and time window, not wall time.

Transient low-speed aborts should be retried in-process a bounded number of times so a transient stall self-heals within a single review instead of deferring to backfill; non-low-speed failures (auth, bad ref) must not be retried.
Module repo_snapshot.py at 788/800 LOC has no headroom for the fix, requiring code extraction of the git-subprocess and fetch-locking cluster into a new sibling module git_fetch.py.
